subject: Temporary headroom conversion options for LaunchLab demo
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@launchlab.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: LaunchLab Ops <ops@launchlab.io>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term headroom + convert-to-commit option

Hi Vivek,

We have a product demo to a strategic prospect next week (April 2) and expect a burst of API traffic for a 36-hour window. Our current committed tier will be exceeded unless we get temporary headroom.

Quick questions: can Redwood provision a short-term quota uplift (10x for 36 hours) and surface an option to convert that uplift into a committed discount if we decide to stay at a higher baseline afterwards?

I've attached our recent usage export so you can see the spike profile. Pricing/contract conversations will be with our procurement, but I wanted to get a ballpark and the operational path first.

Thanks,
Sam Ortiz
Head of Platform
LaunchLab

Attachments: usage_report_Mar2028.csv (CSV, 340KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@launchlab.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term headroom + convert-to-commit option

Sam — thanks for the context and the export. I skimmed the spike and it looks like a typical demo-profile burst (short but high QPS). We can support this without code changes. Two practical paths I suggest: 

1) Provisional uplift: We open a 36-hour temporary headroom for the dates you specify. That is provisioned immediately and billed as overrun at the standard overage rate, but we can offer a one-time promo credit to cover part of the uplift for first-time demo bursts (subject to approval). Operationally this is fast — we can enable within a few hours.

2) Convertible commit: If you expect sustained higher baseline after the demo, we can structure a short-term uplift that is convertible into a committed monthly baseline with a retroactive true-up and a blended discount. In practice this means: we provision the uplift, track the additional consumption, and if you sign a commit within 30 days we amortize a portion of the uplift charges into the commit and apply a discounted unit rate going forward.

Ben — can you draft a compact quote for both options (provisional uplift with promo credit and a convertible 3-month commit with blended discount)? Laura — please flag any procurement/PO requirements that would slow the convertible flow.

Sam — I'll keep this thread as the operational lane. If we need legal language for the convert clause we'll loop them in after Ben has a draft.

—Vivek
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@launchlab.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term headroom + convert-to-commit option

Sam / Vivek — thanks. Sam, attaching a concise proposal PDF in this thread (LaunchLab_proposal_20280328.pdf). Summary of the two options we propose: 

- Option A (Provisional uplift):
  * 36-hour uplift to 10x baseline starting 2028-04-02 00:00 PDT
  * Standard overrun rate: $0.045/token (applies to uplift volume)
  * One-time demo promo credit: $2,500 applied to overrun invoice if uplift is requested by 2028-03-30
  * No PO required for provisional uplift; billing will appear on next invoice unless you request net-30.

- Option B (Convertible 3-month commit):
  * Provision same uplift window immediately.
  * If LaunchLab signs a 3-month commit within 30 days, we will: retroactively credit 50% of uplift overrun fees into the commit, and apply a blended unit price equal to a 12% discount off list for the duration of the commit.
  * Requires PO and signed SOW; target turnaround 5–10 business days for standard procurement.

Operational notes: we will instrument a temporary routing rule so traffic hits an ephemeral capacity pool to guarantee latency SLOs during the demo. If you want immediate enablement, confirm the start date/time and I'll ask infra to flip the switch.

Next steps: Sam — please confirm which option you prefer and whether your procurement team needs an emailed quote or a DocuSign. If you want Option B, we should get procurement contact details and a PO template so Laura can prep the SOW with the correct billing terms.

—Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: LaunchLab_proposal_20280328.pdf (Proposal, 28 pages)

From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@launchlab.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: LaunchLab Ops <ops@launchlab.io>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term headroom + convert-to-commit option

Thanks, Vivek and Ben — this is exactly what we needed.

We'd like to go with Option B (Convertible 3-month commit). Key asks:
- Please send the DocuSign so procurement can sign the SOW quickly (PO process at LaunchLab is ~3 business days once we have a doc).
- Confirm the uplift start: 2028-04-02 00:00 PDT (we'll allocate our demo traffic to that window).
- We'll share the procurement contact and PO template by end of day.

Appreciate the flexibility on the retroactive credit — that makes the convert path much easier to justify internally.

Sam Ortiz
Head of Platform
LaunchLab
